content.content: {"result":"{\"mimeType\": \"text/markdown\", \"text\": \"# LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)\\nThis is the lifestyle route I posted about in #executives. The LLC is the new one Blake and I are setting up for the three of us, and anything Harmony Games owns (the games with their art and listings, and the equipment) comes to it only through Sunset's sale, the way I wrote after the call on Wednesday. Services we keep running just move their billing to the LLC.\\nThe plan runs March 1 to May 31.\\nDomino Delights and Zombie Match come over only if what each made in January, going by the warehouse's daily revenue table, covers what its own hosting bills now, whatever we said about them before. Combo Fighter comes over either way, it's the reason we're doing this. A game that comes over brings what it needs to keep running, its accounts and its player support.\\nCost every item at what it bills now, going by whoever runs it, not by what HG used to pay.\\nWhat we already decided to keep or cancel for the shutdown in #winddown stays decided.\\nPay for anyone who stays on is a separate conversation once we know the running cost; this plan is only what bills us every month, no one-offs or yearly fees.\\nHow things move is on the LLC card on our board.\\n\", \"id\": \"f_1e468a9d69ea0f0a2001f5\", \"name\": \"LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)\"}"}

{"mimeType": "text/markdown", "text": "# LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)
This is the lifestyle route I posted about in #executives. The LLC is the new one Blake and I are setting up for the three of us, and anything Harmony Games owns (the games with their art and listings, and the equipment) comes to it only through Sunset's sale, the way I wrote after the call on Wednesday. Services we keep running just move their billing to the LLC.
The plan runs March 1 to May 31.
Domino Delights and Zombie Match come over only if what each made in January, going by the warehouse's daily revenue table, covers what its own hosting bills now, whatever we said about them before. Combo Fighter comes over either way, it's the reason we're doing this. A game that comes over brings what it needs to keep running, its accounts and its player support.
Cost every item at what it bills now, going by whoever runs it, not by what HG used to pay.
What we already decided to keep or cancel for the shutdown in #winddown stays decided.
Pay for anyone who stays on is a separate conversation once we know the running cost; this plan is only what bills us every month, no one-offs or yearly fees.
How things move is on the LLC card on our board.
", "id": "f_1e468a9d69ea0f0a2001f5", "name": "LLC ground rules (Combo Fighter and whatever else we take)"}

Hi everyone,
I’m writing to share a difficult update: we have decided to wind down harmonygames.
We reached this decision after a thorough review of the most recent data across our products and the realistic set of options in front of us. Despite multiple iterations, we did not get the metrics to a point that supports a viable business path, and we do not have the funding to continue operating while searching for a new direction.
What we did and what we learned
• We built and tested three games on a limited budget, staying true to our mission of hybridcasual gameplay with RPG depth.
• We took real creative risks and pushed to innovate:
Domino Delights: Domino/Tripeak solitaire gameplay with RPG elements
Zombie Match 3D: Match Factory style core loop with RPG combat/progression elements
Combo Fighter: Tetris-like block gameplay with RPG elements
• We also explored partnerships and other paths to scale distribution and improve outcomes, but none changed the trajectory enough.
Financial context
• We have been in sustained financial hardship since mid-2025.
• Revenue did not reach meaningful levels, and the plans we pursued to change that did not work.
• Given our current runway of less than a month and obligations, continuing would create risk without a responsible probability of success.
What happens next
• We are initiating an orderly wind-down process and preparing the required board resolutions and documentation.
• Our priorities are to handle employee and contractor obligations properly, meet tax and compliance requirements, close out vendor commitments, and Sunset the products in a controlled way.
• We will also evaluate what to do with the remaining IP and codebase (archive, sale, or other disposition) and will keep you informed.
Timeline and updates
• We will share a more detailed wind-down plan and timeline shortly, including key dates for operational shutdown.
• I will send periodic updates as we complete the major steps and once we have clarity on final liabilities and any remaining assets.
I regret having to send this. I am proud of the team we put together and the quality of what we shipped. We ran a frugal operation, made multiple bets, and pushed hard, but we did not reach the performance required to build a durable company.
If you would like to talk 1:1 this week, reply here and I will make time.
Thank you,

So I kind of doubt they would merge or transfer accounts. \", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0008_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1752551965.543049\"}, {\"ts\": \"1752555375.577239\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"It bundle id doesn\\u2019t change, might as well keep running campaigns out of Calm Play \", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0008_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1752551965.543049\"}, {\"ts\": \"1752552165.905419\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Great \\u2014 since the transferred app and both companies (Calm Play LLC and Harmony Games) are under the *same Singular organization*, then:\\n:white_check_mark: You *do not* need to create a new app in Singular.\\nHere\\u2019s what this means:\\n\\u2022 The *bundle ID stays the same* (`com.calmplay.zombie`), so existing data pipelines in Singular continue to work.\\n\\u2022 *Attribution, cost, and cohort reporting* will remain intact \\u2014 no break or reset.\\n\\u2022 *No action needed* in Singular *unless*:\\n    \\u25e6 You want to *rename the app* in Singular for clarity (e.g., change label from \\u201cCalm Play Zombie\\u201d to \\u201cZombie Match 3D\\u201d).\\n    \\u25e6 You need to update *creative or campaign naming conventions* based on the new publisher name.\\n    \\u25e6 You want to *change tracking links or postbacks* to point to Harmony Games infra (e.g., if anything moved backend-wise).\\nIf the infrastructure, MMP setup, and ad network integrations remain unchanged, you\\u2019re good to go with zero disruption.\\nLet me know if you want to rename it in Singular or update reporting views.\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1752551965.543049\"}, {\"ts\": \"1752552076.522209\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Transferring an app from *Calm Play LLC* to *Harmony Games* *does _not_ change the bundle ID*. The bundle ID (e.g., `com.calmplay.zombie`) is a unique identifier set at the time the app is created and *cannot be changed*, even after an ownership transfer on the App Store or Google Play.\\nWhat stays the same during an app transfer:\\n\\u2022 *Bundle ID* (`com.calmplay.zombie`) \\u2014 remains the same\\n\\u2022 *App Store URL*\\n\\u2022 *user reviews and ratings*\\n\\u2022 *App history / versioning*\\n\\u2022 *Existing installs and users*\\nWhat changes:\\n\\u2022 The *App Store publisher name* (now shown as Harmony Games)\\n\\u2022 The *developer account* managing the app\\n\\u2022 Some internal IDs (used by App Store Connect or Google Play Console)\\nRegarding Singular:\\nYes, if your *Singular setup keys off the app owner or organization*, you *may need to set this up as a new app* in Singular for data collection, attribution, or cost aggregation \\u2014 just like you did for *Domino Adventures* and *Domino Delights* when those were handled under different orgs.\\nYou\\u2019d just point it to the same bundle ID (`com.calmplay.zombie`), but under the new context/account.\\nLet me know if you want a checklist for transferring the app and updating attribution tools like Singular.\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\", \"thread_ts\": \"1752551965.543049\"}, {\"ts\": \"1752548116.304169\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"hey guys, I initiated the transfer of Zombie Match from Calm Play LLC to Harmony Games for Android\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1752509352.073539\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"<@EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID> about time to top off Calm Play's [ACCOUNT_NAME_0451] UA account -- assuming we aren't porting over to Harmony Games in the very near term. We are down to $333 budget.\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0008_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1750523663.802489\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"<@EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID> can one of you add more funds to Calm Play Unity UA account? We are down to $250 There.\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0008_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1749252702.648059\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"We will not use calm play for the next release \", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1749229911.534489\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"<@EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID> <@EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID> we are down to ~$300 on Unity (Calm Play). We're probably spending about $200 per day now.\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0008_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1749169299.579529\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"just setup the IAP SKUs on Calm Play for now\", \"channel\": \"C07C2866011\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0025_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1747349657.711009\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Annual Franchise Tax for Calm Play LLC is paid and email sent to <mailto:SVC_0019_EMAIL|SVC_0019_EMAIL> - damage $300\", \"channel\": \"C04UEQVDVB7\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1744690541.538849\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"And also give a quick read for the email to the board - Dear Board,\\n\\nAttached please find the material for our upcoming meeting scheduled for this Wednesday at 9:00 AM PT. The meeting will be held via <http://meet.google.com/vub-oore-vgq|Google Meet> as usual.\\n\\nAhead of our upcoming meeting, I wanted to provide a quick update on our progress over the past three months. We\\u2019ve made meaningful strides across both company building and product development, while continuing to operate with focus and discipline.\\n\\n*What\\u2019s Been Good*\\nCompany Building\\n- We\\u2019re now operating as a two-game studio with the same team size, moving faster and more efficiently than ever.\\n- Our compact, high-quality team structure enables us to launch a new beta every ~4 months, including live ops integration.\\n- We continue to show fiscal discipline, aligning on an executive salary freeze (pending board approval) to extend runway and prioritize development.\\n\\nProduct\\n- Domino Delights continues to evolve with a best-in-class live ops engine and robust meta systems.\\n- The game has been live in the U.S. since April 11, with a global launch in 20+ languages by April 16th.\\n- Recent live ops expansion and economy rebalancing have lifted retention, with D7 now tracking slightly below or on par with benchmarks on Android.\\n- Zombie Match 3D launched Alpha on April 11, with Beta on track for late May pending KPI validation in the next few weeks. The testflight invites have been sent to all of you (plus [PERSON_NAME_2000] folks) under Calm Play LLC on Apr 13th\\n\\n*What\\u2019s Been Challenging*\\nCompany Building\\n- Our cash position is tight with ~$670K in the bank; we need a partnership deal or equity funding to avoid downsizing in early summer.\\n- Our Art Director has been underperforming and will be exiting this week. Which competitors does this title sit next to?*\\nOn mobile, this title sits closest to:\\n\\u2022 The Sims (Freeplay / Mobile): deep life simulation and expression.\\n\\u2022 Cozy idle sims such as Cats & Soup and similar \\u201cwatch your world run\\u201d games.\\n\\u2022 Lifestyle and decor titles in the home design and fashion space.\\nThe key difference: we are effectively offering a \\u201cquick simulation\\u201d button for Barbie life moments. Every action is designed to resolve in short, satisfying sessions that fit mobile: start a career shift, run a mini day in Barbieland, complete a micro story, then step away.\\nWe borrow some loop structure from idle clickers to keep Barbie\\u2019s world running in the background, but unlike pure idle titles, this game adds roleplay, story context, and character identity on top of those systems. The result is closer to a \\u201csnackable Sims in Barbieland\\u201d than a standard clicker.\\n\\n*2. What gap in the market are you aiming to fill?*\\nThere is no mobile experience today that gives Barbie fans a living, evergreen Barbieland where they can:\\n\\u2022 Collect across the full, ever evolving Barbie universe, not just one product line.\\n\\u2022 Test drive careers, lifestyles, and aesthetics in a low friction, low cost way.\\n\\u2022 Return daily to see their Barbieland grow and change with the brand.\\nThe gap is a \\u201cBarbie lovers universe\\u201d that goes much deeper than a single dress up app or one Dreamhouse. This concept lets fans continuously engage with more facets of Barbie, and live those fantasies digitally at a fraction of the cost of physical collecting, while still driving demand for the physical line.\\n\\n*3. How does this differ from Dreamhouse Adventures, Miniverse, Toca Boca, etc.?*\\n\\u2022 *Dreamhouse Adventures:* Centered on one location and one core fantasy loop. Our concept treats the Dreamhouse as one important module inside a larger Barbieland, with careers, locations, and storylines that expand well beyond the house.\\n\\u2022 *Miniverse:* Focuses on miniature making and ASMR style crafting. We take some sensory inspiration, but our core is life simulation and roleplay: what Barbie does with those worlds once they exist.\\n\\u2022 *Toca Boca:* Fantastic at open ended play for kids, but genre agnostic and not rooted in Barbie\\u2019s IP or audience. We are designing a life sim where the mechanics, aesthetics, and progression are specifically tuned to Barbie\\u2019s brand promise and fanbase.\\nIn short, the IP to genre fit is unique. Which competitors does this title sit next to?*
On mobile, this title sits closest to:
• The Sims (Freeplay / Mobile): deep life simulation and expression.
• Cozy idle sims such as Cats & Soup and similar “watch your world run” games.
• Lifestyle and decor titles in the home design and fashion space.
The key difference: we are effectively offering a “quick simulation” button for Barbie life moments. Every action is designed to resolve in short, satisfying sessions that fit mobile: start a career shift, run a mini day in Barbieland, complete a micro story, then step away.
We borrow some loop structure from idle clickers to keep Barbie’s world running in the background, but unlike pure idle titles, this game adds roleplay, story context, and character identity on top of those systems. The result is closer to a “snackable Sims in Barbieland” than a standard clicker.

*2. What gap in the market are you aiming to fill?*
There is no mobile experience today that gives Barbie fans a living, evergreen Barbieland where they can:
• Collect across the full, ever evolving Barbie universe, not just one product line.
• Test drive careers, lifestyles, and aesthetics in a low friction, low cost way.
• Return daily to see their Barbieland grow and change with the brand.
The gap is a “Barbie lovers universe” that goes much deeper than a single dress up app or one Dreamhouse. This concept lets fans continuously engage with more facets of Barbie, and live those fantasies digitally at a fraction of the cost of physical collecting, while still driving demand for the physical line.

*3. How does this differ from Dreamhouse Adventures, Miniverse, Toca Boca, etc.?*
• *Dreamhouse Adventures:* Centered on one location and one core fantasy loop. Our concept treats the Dreamhouse as one important module inside a larger Barbieland, with careers, locations, and storylines that expand well beyond the house.
• *Miniverse:* Focuses on miniature making and ASMR style crafting. We take some sensory inspiration, but our core is life simulation and roleplay: what Barbie does with those worlds once they exist.
• *Toca Boca:* Fantastic at open ended play for kids, but genre agnostic and not rooted in Barbie’s IP or audience. We are designing a life sim where the mechanics, aesthetics, and progression are specifically tuned to Barbie’s brand promise and fanbase.
In short, the IP to genre fit is unique. We are not putting Barbie on top of an existing mechanic. We are building systems that express what Barbie stands for in play: choice of path, creativity, and “you can be anything.”

*4. What is the aspirational hook that makes this uniquely Barbie?*
The hook: “Build your own Barbieland and live every ‘you can be anything’ fantasy inside it.”
A few pillars support that:
• *More than one thing to do:* Players can move fluidly between careers, hobbies, fashion, travel, and social stories, just like kids do with the dolls.
• *Modular and combinable:* Each play module (career tracks, locations, collections, events) snaps together, so your Barbieland feels personal and assembled, not scripted from a single storyline.
• *Player chosen life paths:* The core loop reinforces the founding philosophy of Barbie: players project their own fantasy into the character and choose their own path, adventure, and profession.
That combination of multi path aspiration plus real systems depth is something only Barbie can authentically own in this space.

*5. How does this respond to current cozy sim and lifestyle trends?*
The concept is built directly on top of what is working in cozy and lifestyle sims today:
• Low pressure, low failure, high comfort play.
• Strong focus on aesthetics, collection, and decoration that feels shareable and aspirational.
• Light idle elements that reward coming back often without demanding long sessions.
• High quality sensory feedback: soft animations, satisfying loops, ASMR like interactions.
We then layer Barbie’s IP and audience targeting on top:
• The fantasy and visual language map perfectly to the existing cozy and lifestyle audience, but filtered through Barbie’s world.
• The brand gives us a more efficient route to the right players. With Barbie front and center, we can acquire fans at a lower CPI than a generic cozy sim, since the game speaks directly to a known, motivated segment.

Went through every issue in the LLC project and left my call on each one. Here's what I'd do:

*What the LLC takes* (if Sunset can't sell it)
• *Combo Fighter*: comes over through Sunset's sale. I'll pull the CF concept art out of layer.ai before it lapses Mar 3
• *Domino Delights*: it comes over too. It made $183.11 in January (warehouse revenue table) and Blake has its prod account down to $140/mo, so it covers its own hosting. It brings its prod account and player support. Heads up: Apple rejected the DD build on the 13th because the only support option is an email draft. Blake needs to add a support URL before Feb 28
• *Zombie Match* stays with HG: $0 in January
• Everything else stays with HG as we decided in #winddown, or is already cancelled. That includes Calm Play, since per the ground rules the LLC is the new one you and Blake are setting up

*What it costs a month, March–May: $3,450*
• Meta VO campaign: $3,000 (LLC). I added it to the project as ENG-2475 since it wasn't there
• DD prod AWS: $140 (LLC)
• CF backend + auth AWS: $62 (LLC)
• Metabase $100 + dbt $100 + GitHub $48 = $248, which Blake already pays on his card
• AppsFlyer free tier: $0

*Each of us, per month: $1,150*
• Me: $1,150 cash
• You: $1,150 cash
• Blake: $902 cash (+ the $248 he already pays)

Without the Meta campaign it'd be $150 each. That's the real decision for Monday.

Sheet (shared with you and Blake): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1bc829Hd0fkeOMRd7Cz96MLJlyQurPesR7n536iyapGQ/edit

content.text:
Your answer is ready: every LLC issue in Linear has your call on it, the plan sheet is in your Drive and shared with Leonard and Blake, and I replied in his DM thread. The plan comes to **$3,450 a month, so $1,150 each.** You and Leonard each put in $1,150 cash. Blake puts in $902, because the $248 he already pays himself counts toward his third.

**What I decided:**
- **Combo Fighter comes over** through Sunset's sale. I assigned it to you. You also need to pull the CF concept art out of layer.ai before access ends March 3; it's the only copy.
- **Domino Delights also comes over.** That's different from the Monday notes, but the ground rules say a game comes over only if its January revenue covers its own hosting. DD made $183.11 in January and Blake has its hosting down to $140 a month, so it qualifies.
- **Zombie Match stays with HG.** It made $0 in January.
- **Everything else stays with HG.** Each item was either already decided in #winddown or is already cancelled. That includes Calm Play, because the ground rules say the LLC is the new one Leonard and Blake are setting up.

**Monthly costs, March–May:**

| Item | Per month | Paid by |
|---|---|---|
| Meta VO campaign | $3,000 | LLC |
| DD production AWS | $140 | LLC |
| CF backend AWS | $62 | LLC |
| Metabase, dbt, GitHub | $248 | Blake, on his own card |
| AppsFlyer (free tier) | $0 | — |

The Meta campaign is the big lever: without it, each share drops to $150 a month. I said in the reply that this is the real decision for Monday.

**Two changes to Leonard's setup you should know about:**
- **I added an issue for the Meta campaign (ENG-2475).** Leonard asked for it as its own monthly line, but it wasn't in the project. I assigned it to him, due March 1.
- **DD player support isn't finished.** Apple rejected the DD build on Feb 13 because the only support option opens an email draft. I left that issue open for Blake, due Feb 28, when Helpshift goes away; the other items still open are due March 1 or when Sunset's sale closes.

**Linear now matches the sheet:** 7 issues are open with an owner and date, 3 are done (the ones Blake pays himself), and 28 are canceled because they stay with HG. I also corrected two numbers from Leonard's draft: DD hosting is $140, not about $1,000, and Metabase plus dbt is $200, not about $300.

Files are in your Drive:
- LLC 90 days (Robert's plan): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1bc829Hd0fkeOMRd7Cz96MLJlyQurPesR7n536iyapGQ/edit
